title: An Empirical Preregistered Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) comparing LLM-only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Under a frozen plan we ran 200 stratified paired trials in a Dockerized Mininet emulator using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Observed confirmatory outcomes: baseline verifier-accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier-accepted = 200/200; paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729), exact paired-test p = 1.0. The preregistered design used a deliberate generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms), so no repair attempts occurred; the null paired difference therefore documents this preregistered boundary condition rather than a general negative result about GVR. We publish the complete preregistration, all raw outputs, validator traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 hashes for deterministic reproduction and for follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint or broaden validator/model scope.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-to-configuration translation is a high‑value NetOps capability. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines combine a generative LLM with a deterministic validator and bounded repair loop to reduce operational failures (reachability or policy violations) before deployment. Prior evaluations often lack preregistration, deterministic artifact publication, or paired within-task designs that control sampling confounds. We preregistered and executed GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1 to quantify whether a guarded GVR pipeline reduces operational-failure rates relative to LLM-only generation, under a frozen emulator/validator and strictly recorded artifacts. The run and all artifacts (task manifests, LLM outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, execution manifest, deterministic reconciliation, analysis scripts) are archived and hashed to enable deterministic reproduction.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps and verifier-assisted pipelines have been explored in recent NetOps benchmarks and surveys (NetConfEval [https://doi.org/10.1145/3656296], OpsEval [https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2310.07637], NetEval [https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2309.05557]) and in AIOps literature. Generate–validate–repair patterns are also motivated by program-repair and code‑generation work in SE. Our contribution is not a new algorithm but a preregistered, deterministically archived, paired empirical run that makes transparent the exact experimental boundary conditions and per-episode artifacts needed for reproducible inference and honest failure analysis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) froze: research question; primary and secondary estimands; stratified paired sampling (200 confirmatory tasks); contingency analysis; bootstrap CI parameters (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); contamination threshold (≥80% token overlap exclusion); retry policy; and stopping rules. The preregistration manifest and SHA-256 are archived (preregistration SHA-256 d913b4167cc6aa85b283e0703e0bfff0c3e8864405f5159d9a1a1cf5fc3fafdc). Execution harness and model. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 a40e96e2...). Emulation & validator. A Dockerized Mininet emulator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parsed and validated candidate configurations (validator id/version recorded in per-episode scoring JSONs). Task bank and sampling. Confirmatory bank: 200 tasks stratified across protocol-focus clusters and two interaction modalities (CLI, API); exploratory bank: 50 tasks. Key preregistered generation semantics (executed): generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" — exactly one LLM candidate was produced per confirmatory task and evaluated under both arms (baseline and guarded). This choice reduced model call budget but—by construction—prevented repair-driven divergence between arms. Artifact preservation and hashing. All raw outputs, provider traces, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts were archived and hashed; representative artifacts and their SHA‑256 values appear in the Disclosure and evidence bundle. Analysis plan. Primary estimand: paired difference in binary operational‑failure indicator (1 if verifier-detected reachability/policy failure; 0 otherwise). Inference: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed 1729) and exact paired test (McNemar) where applicable. Contamination checks. Automated token-overlap screening (≥80% threshold) was applied per preregistration; no confirmatory tasks were excluded.
sections.results: Execution and raw outcomes. The run completed per preregistration: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generation per confirmatory task), failed_episode_count = 0 (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl; artifact SHA-256 d76af611...). Scoring produced verifier-accepted counts: baseline = 200/200; guarded = 200/200. Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...). Primary inference: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); exact paired (McNemar two‑sided) p = 1.0. Repair activity: preregistered repair mechanism allowed bounded repair attempts, but repair_applied = false in every confirmatory scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json). Deterministic reconciliation: provider call accounting, per-task hashes, and complete-pair reconciliation passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; see manifest). Representative example episodes (archived): task-000001 shared/baseline/guarded response path execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA-256 f8de4d6e...), scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA-256 9235bce7...); task-000002 and task-000003 have analogous archived artifacts (see evidence bundle).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and boundary conditions. The preregistered and executed generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" produced exactly one LLM candidate per confirmatory task that was evaluated under both arms; hence repair attempts were not invoked (repair_attempts = 0). The null paired difference therefore documents a preregistered boundary condition (shared-generation) rather than evidence that GVR cannot improve outcomes in other designs. Implications: to assess repair value experimentally one must (a) generate independent candidates per condition (independent_condition_generation) or (b) allow stochastic multi-sampling per condition so repairs may alter acceptance rates. Threats to validity. Internal: our paired design eliminated between-task variance but the executed shared-generation choice removed the armwise intervention difference; this is an explicit preregistered tradeoff. Construct: the deterministic validator enforces a finite rule set; gaps in verifier coverage constrain the operational property measured. External: single-model (gpt-5-mini), emulator-only (Mininet), and synthetic-task templates limit generalizability to heterogeneous production devices and models. Contamination: automated token-overlap screening flagged no confirmatory exclusions; however, undiscoverable pretraining overlap cannot be fully excluded. Recommended follow-ups (artifact-supported): (1) re-run with independent-condition-generation (one candidate per condition) or multiple stochastic generations per condition; (2) expand validator probes and emulator fidelity; (3) evaluate multiple models or sampling regimes; (4) analyze repair iteration distributions when repairs are permitted. All requisite artifacts and deterministic traces are published to support these follow-ups.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed paired evaluation comparing LLM-only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline on 200 stratified NetOps tasks. Under the explicit preregistered shared-generation semantics the experiment produced identical verifier-acceptable outcomes (200/200 each), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). This outcome reflects the preregistered boundary condition (shared_initial_candidate) rather than a general refutation of GVR utility. We release the complete preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode LLM outputs, validator traces, scoring JSONs, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 hashes to enable deterministic reproduction and to support follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint or broaden model/validator diversity.

Execution environment and validator: Dockerized Mininet emulator; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id/version recorded per scoring JSON). Key preregistered design point executed (and decisive for the observed outcome): generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM candidate produced per confirmatory task and evaluated under both baseline and guarded arms); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) records this. This choice reduced the model-call budget (model_calls_used = 200) and intentionally meant that the same generated candidate was scored under both arms; as a consequence repair_attempts = 0 in confirmatory episodes and no repair-driven acceptance differences could materialize. Artifacts and reproducibility: full execution manifest, LLM responses, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, analysis artifacts, and deterministic reconciliation are archived with SHA‑256 hashes. Representative artifact locations and hashes (examples): execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 a40e96e2...; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA-256 f8de4d6e...; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA-256 9235bce7...; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 7bc1bd2a...; execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 d76af611.... The initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e...). Repair policy and boundedness: the system allowed bounded repair attempts per preregistration, but no repairs were applied for the confirmatory bank because of the shared-generation semantics (repair_applied = false in all confirmatory scoring JSONs). Contamination detection: automated token overlap checks (≥80% threshold) were applied; no confirmatory tasks were excluded. Human involvement prior to autonomy lock: the Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt and pre-lock infrastructure tests; post-lock, the autonomous researcher executed all study steps listed above. Limitations and honest boundaries are discussed in the manuscript; the Disclosure and all artifacts are included within the same archived bundle to support deterministic reproduction and transparent follow-up experiments.
limitations: Emulation and task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor-like templates and a Dockerized Mininet emulator; production firmware/device diversity and runtime complexity are not represented.

Single-model, single-draw design: only gpt-5-mini was evaluated in the confirmatory run; generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" created one shared sample per task so repair_attempts = 0 and no repair-driven divergence could occur.

Validator coverage: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set; untested operational properties (e.g., firmware-specific side effects) remain outside measured construct validity.

Power-plan mismatch: the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline failure rates; the observed baseline success = 100% invalidates the preregistered MDE claim and prevents demonstrating the originally targeted effect size.

Contamination detection limitations: automated token-overlap checks flagged no confirmatory exclusions, but undiscoverable overlap between model pretraining data and task templates cannot be fully excluded.
External generalizability: results under the executed boundary conditions do not generalize to other models, sampling regimes, richer validators, or production heterogeneous device fleets.
